On this day in 1918, an armistice was signed ending fighting in World War I.
On this day in 1912, the bodies of Captain Robert Falcon Scott and his companions were found in Antarctica after their doomed expedition.
On this day in 1982, the Vietnam Veterans Memorial was dedicated in Washington, D.C.
On this day in 1851, Herman Melville's novel 'Moby-Dick' was first published in the United States.

header: Sherman's March to the Sea Begins
message: On this day in 1864, Union General William Tecumseh Sherman began his destructive March to the Sea during the Civil War.
On this day in 1907, Oklahoma was admitted as the 46th U.S. state.
On this day in 1869, the Suez Canal officially opened, connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas.
On this day in 1978, over 900 members of the Peoples Temple died in a mass murder-suicide in Jonestown, Guyana.
On this day in 1863, President Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address at the dedication of a Civil War cemetery.
On this day in 1945, the Nuremberg trials began, prosecuting Nazi leaders for war crimes.
On this day in 1877, Thomas Edison announced his invention of the phonograph, the first device to record and reproduce sound.
On this day in 1963, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas, Texas.
On this day in 1936, the first issue of the photojournalism magazine Life was published.
On this day in 1859, Charles Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species,' introducing the theory of evolution by natural selection.
On this day in 1867, Alfred Nobel was granted a patent for dynamite.

header: First Thanksgiving Proclaimed a National Holiday
message: On this day in 1789, President Washington proclaimed the first Thanksgiving Day under the new U.S. Constitution.
On this day in 1895, Alfred Nobel signed his will, establishing the Nobel Prizes.
On this day in 1943, Allied leaders Churchill, Roosevelt, and Stalin met for the first time at the Tehran Conference.
On this day in 1947, the United Nations General Assembly voted to partition Palestine into Jewish and Arab states.
On this day in 1954, a meteorite struck and injured a woman in Sylacauga, Alabama, one of the few documented cases of a person being hit by a meteorite.

header: Rosa Parks Refuses to Give Up Her Seat
message: On this day in 1955, Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger, sparking the Montgomery Bus Boycott.
On this day in 1804, Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of France in Notre-Dame Cathedral.
On this day in 1984, a toxic gas leak at a pesticide plant in Bhopal, India, killed thousands of people.

header: Washington Bids Farewell to His Officers
message: On this day in 1783, George Washington bade farewell to his officers at Fraunces Tavern in New York City.
On this day in 1933, the 21st Amendment was ratified, repealing Prohibition in the United States.
On this day in 1865, the 13th Amendment was ratified, abolishing slavery throughout the United States.
On this day in 1941, Japanese forces launched a surprise attack on the U.S. naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
On this day in 1980, musician John Lennon was shot and killed outside his New York City apartment.
On this day in 1961, Tanganyika gained independence from British colonial rule, later becoming part of Tanzania.
On this day in 1901, the first Nobel Prizes were awarded in Stockholm, Sweden.
On this day in 1936, King Edward VIII abdicated the British throne to marry Wallis Simpson.
On this day in 1901, Guglielmo Marconi received the first transatlantic radio signal in Newfoundland, Canada.
On this day in 1937, Japanese forces captured Nanjing, China, beginning a brutal period known as the Nanjing Massacre.
On this day in 1911, Roald Amundsen and his team became the first to reach the South Pole.
On this day in 1791, the Bill of Rights was ratified, becoming part of the U.S. Constitution.
On this day in 1773, American colonists boarded British ships and dumped tea into Boston Harbor to protest taxation.
On this day in 1903, the Wright brothers achieved the first sustained, powered flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
On this day in 1865, the 13th Amendment was officially adopted, formally abolishing slavery in the United States.

header: Washington's Army Winters at Valley Forge
message: On this day in 1777, General Washington's Continental Army arrived at Valley Forge to endure a harsh winter encampment.
On this day in 1803, the United States formally took possession of the Louisiana Purchase territory from France.
On this day in 1913, the first crossword puzzle was published in the New York World newspaper.
On this day in 1944, General Anthony McAuliffe famously replied 'Nuts!' to a German surrender demand during the Battle of the Bulge.
On this day in 1947, scientists at Bell Labs successfully demonstrated the first working transistor.

header: Christmas Eve Truce of World War I
message: On this day in 1914, soldiers on the Western Front held an unofficial truce, briefly halting fighting for the Christmas holiday.
On this day in 1776, General Washington led his troops across the Delaware River in a surprise attack on Trenton.
On this day in 2004, a massive undersea earthquake triggered a tsunami that killed over 230,000 people across the Indian Ocean region.
On this day in 1979, Soviet forces invaded Afghanistan, beginning a decade-long conflict.
On this day in 1846, Iowa was admitted as the 29th U.S. state.
On this day in 1890, U.S. troops killed hundreds of Lakota men, women, and children at Wounded Knee, South Dakota.
On this day in 1922, the Soviet Union was officially established with the signing of a founding treaty.
On this day in 1954, Ellis Island closed its doors after processing millions of immigrants over six decades.
